summary: Media transport row: previous, a filled play/pause that cross-fades as it flips, next, and optionally shuffle and repeat with three clearly different states (off grey, all a tinted disc, one a solid disc). Each control sends its own host action, flips its own state at once and tells a screen reader its state; shuffle and repeat drop out when the window is narrow.

playing.doc: 1 while playing. Bind an exported variable: the tap flips it at once and the app's next write wins

repeat.doc: 0 off, 1 all, 2 one; a tap cycles 0, 1, 2

size.doc: The play face: 72, 64 or 48 dp. All other targets stay 48 dp. small is for widgets

skip.doc: tracks: previous and next. seconds: back 10 and forward 30, for podcasts and audiobooks (onPrevious, onNext still fire)

previous.doc: false: no previous control, for a mini player

secondaryAt.doc: Window width in dp under which shuffle and repeat drop out, leaving the three main controls

color.doc: Play face and the on state of shuffle and repeat

onPlayPause.doc: Host action for play/pause. Read the new state from the bound variable, or give each state its own handling in the app

onShuffle.doc: Host action for shuffle. Omitted: no shuffle control

onRepeat.doc: Host action for repeat. Omitted: no repeat control

pitfalls: Host action names must differ per control when the document must also convert with the Java parser (U58): playPause, previous, next, shuffle, repeat
The tap writes the bound variable first, so the icon flips at once; the app then confirms by writing the same variable. An app that refuses the change just writes it back

To send a state to the app, carry it: {"type": "hostNamedAction", "name": "repeat", "value": "@repeat", "valueType": "float", "actionType": 0} (both keys: json2rc reads valueType, the Java parser actionType, same bytes)

It fills the width it is given and spaces its controls evenly: three controls need 144 dp at size small, 160 at medium, five need 256 at medium. secondaryAt is compared with the WINDOW, so in a side-by-side pane raise it: secondaryAt can be an expression. Under 140 dp of window only play/pause stays
One call per document is the normal case. Its label variables are shared names (tcPlayLabel, tcShufLabel, tcRepLabel): two calls with different state would read each other's label on the first frame
Screen reader: Play or Pause as a live label; shuffle reads On or Off as state, repeat Off, All or One track. Mono: state by shape, ring for on and a solid disc for repeat one. No motion in mono
